source.title: Progress Measures for Grokking on Real-world Datasets

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some numerical values are shown only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking on real-world datasets and presents an experiment in which test generalization occurs while the L2 weight norm increases, challenging a weight-norm explanation. It also proposes and plots alternative progress measures.
record.gate_note: The paper’s numerical trajectories are mostly figure-only. It cites prior work for some motivating claims; those cited results are not recorded here. Appendix C reports that adding dropout removes delayed generalization, and Appendix D presents IMDb trajectories.
record.test_reason: On MNIST (MLP) and IMDb (LSTM) it reports grokking in an Omnigrok-style regime. It runs a modified loss under which grokking occurs while the L2 weight norm rises, directly arguing against a weight-norm account. A dropout run removes the delay.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a decreasing L2 weight norm is not required or causal for grokking on real-world data; they 'prove' this from one modified-loss MNIST run. They propose activation sparsity, absolute weight entropy and approximate local circuit complexity as measures that correlate with grokking better than weight norm. They also report that dropout removes delayed generalization. They call the IMDb results limited.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies grokking-style training to MNIST and IMDb classification rather than small algorithmic datasets, introduces three different progress measures, and adds a negative squared-L2 term to induce increasing weight norm in one MNIST run.
record.method_sensitivity: The modified loss with δ = 2e−10 produces grokking while the norm increases; adding dropout at p = 0.3 removes delayed generalization. The paper also reports results across MNIST and IMDb, using different model architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation sparsity plateaus right before grokking. Absolute weight entropy drops sharply with generalization and is flat during overfitting. A KL-under-10%-weight-zeroing score is claimed to track generalization on MNIST and IMDb.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic weight- and activation-statistic progress measures (sparsity, weight entropy, perturbation sensitivity) track or precede grokking on real-world data better than weight norm.

record.problems: Most trajectories are provided only as plots, with no numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The authors describe the IMDb results as limited. Appendix A lists MSELoss, while the main text describes the setup as using cross-entropy loss.

untested.parts: No small algorithmic datasets; no training-set-size dependence of the delay.
No generalizing circuit is identified and no removal of memorizing components is shown. The proposed generic measures are not shown to lead the jump.
No initialization-scale sweep and no lazy-to-rich analysis. Init scale stays at 8.0 throughout. No molecules.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking are not tested. It is unclear whether AdamW weight decay stays on in the modified run.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not examined.

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is figure-only, from single runs, with no uncertainty estimates. δ=2e−10 was found by a manual search. Appendix A lists MSELoss while the text says cross-entropy. The stronger 'not causative' claim rests on one run, and it is unclear whether weight decay was retained there. Linking the progress measures to V2 was rejected because they do not measure circuits and are mostly coincident with, not ahead of, the jump.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses MNIST and IMDb, not small algorithmic datasets; it does not test the training-set-size dependence of the delay.

It measures activation sparsity, absolute weight entropy and approximate local circuit complexity around generalization, but does not identify a Fourier/generalizing circuit or show memorizing components being removed.

It tests real-world datasets and a modified loss that increases weight norm during grokking, and reports a dropout condition without delayed generalization. It does not sweep initialization scale or establish a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
It challenges the necessity of decreasing weight norm, but does not test circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not compare learned algorithms across runs, architectures or hyperparameters.
It does not investigate adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

source_check.notes: The source is titled Progress Measures for Grokking on Real-world Tasks. Its prose specifies cross-entropy, whereas Appendix A lists MSELoss; the actual base loss is unresolved, and trajectory uncertainty is not reported.

statements.correction: MNIST: 3-layer, width-200 ReLU MLP; L′ = L − δΣ|w|²; δ = 2e−10; grokking with increasing norm. Section 3 specifies AdamW with weight decay; Table 1 gives 0.01. Relative circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking are not tested.
statements.problem: The increasing-norm MNIST result is correct, but it challenges required total-norm contraction rather than V5's stated relative-efficiency mechanism. The described setup retains AdamW weight decay; no removal is reported.
